title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Exchange Departure Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Exchange Departure Board
options.lineage: Split-flap quotation boards on mid-century stock exchange floors
options.thesis: Every strategy gets a row on the board, and the board flips its claim to the tested number.
options.viewport: A full-width board: the headline set in flap cells, a working strategy input row, and example rows flipping from claimed to tested.
options.risk: Becomes a novelty if the flaps animate everywhere; the flip must stay a quiet reveal.

raised.raise: Row states restyle a row (amber for caution, dim red for a failed check) without breaking the grid.
Every run is a permanent record: results join the board as new rows and are never silently overwritten.
Depth only from stacked flat panels: no shadows, glows, or gradients anywhere.
One accent is reserved for whatever is running right now.
Headlines do the shouting in big condensed type; everything else sits in hard, disciplined columns.
In every chart the chosen line burns brightest and every other line recedes.

options.label: Strategy Facts Label
options.thesis: Every strategy ships with a facts panel: what it claimed, and what it actually did.
options.viewport: A giant facts panel beside the headline, with a working strategy input above it.
options.risk: Familiar: the facts-label format is a widely reused trope, and most runs in this category would land here.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse Board
options.lineage: Rail station departure boards at rush hour
options.thesis: The page as a station board where every row is a departure.
options.viewport: A rail board of destinations, platforms, and statuses.
options.case: Same mechanics as the assigned board, but a rail station is a weaker match for traders than an exchange floor.
options.kept: Row states restyle a row without breaking the grid.

options.label: Ebru Floated Pigment
options.thesis: Results drawn as pigment displaced across water.
options.viewport: A liquid canvas that combs into a chart.
options.case: Fuses poorly: traders don't recognize marbling, and it blurs the numbers that need to be exact.
options.kept: Every mark is permanent; nothing is silently overwritten.

options.label: Łowicz Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Results built up in layers of cut colored paper.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel built from strategy layers.
options.case: Fuses poorly: folk craft has no tie to markets or testing.
options.kept: Depth only from stacked flat layers, never from shading.

options.label: Paper Automata
options.thesis: A strategy as a procession of moving paper figures.
options.viewport: A crank-driven procession of strategy steps.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful motion undercuts a serious research tool.
options.kept: One accent reserved for whatever is moving right now.

options.label: Penny-Press Broadside
options.thesis: Each test result printed as the day's broadside.
options.viewport: A shouting headline over two hard columns of results.
options.case: Fuses poorly: protest-press energy reads as hype, the opposite of honest results.
options.kept: Big type does the shouting; everything else sits in hard columns.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Strategies drawn as routes across a transit map.
options.viewport: A transit map where each line is a strategy.
options.case: Fuses partly: routes are a clever metaphor, but equity curves are data, not schematics, so clarity suffers.
options.kept: The chosen line burns brightest; everything else recedes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dark product page: headline, two buttons, and a screenshot of the IDE.
canonCard.viewport: A centered headline over the IDE screenshot, with feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other AI tools by design.
